title: [replay r8] feat(desktop): recording detail — title on top, destinations strip, copies from this original
body:
> **Replay of [niway-dev/kaipu-record#465](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/465), run 8** for the code-review benchmark. Same base and head commits as the round-1 replay (a second branch name on the same commit, so the reviewer sees a fresh pull request). Never merged. Method: [wachiman/docs/benchmark](https://github.com/niway-dev/wachiman/tree/main/docs/benchmark).

---

## What

The recording detail page, laid out after Claude Design **Kaipu Export v3**, sections 1 ("Right after recording") and 2 ("Revisited"), with the owner's feedback on top of it.

- **Title row.** The top row is now `← Library`, the title (rename pencil, it gets the whole width the row leaves and ellipsizes only at that edge) and the `MASTER · FULL QUALITY` tag. The title used to share a row with the action buttons and got cut off as buttons were added. The tag wording is unchanged; the owner still has to decide on that.
- **Metadata** under the title: Local · age · duration · resolution (once the file is read) · size · N copies.
- **Actions** under the player hold only buttons and wrap when the row grows.
- **Before the first copy.** A fresh recording gets a dismissable green "Saved to your Library…" notice. At the bottom, a **Where is it going?** panel has one equal card per destination: logo, name, short line, and the size of its copy (amber for upload destinations, teal for light ones). A card opens Prepare on that destination through `preparePath`. **Not now** hides the panel and brings back **Export a copy**. The panel replaces the "Where is this going?" strip from #457.
- **With copies.** A pink **Export a copy** button leads the actions; it replaces "Send to…". At the bottom, **Copies from this original** has **Open in Export →** and lists the copies two to a row: logo, name, "2560 × 1440 · 566 MB" or "Exporting · 38% · 2 min left" with a bar, ✓ Ready, and a **Drag** handle. Drag starts a native file drag through the existing `startFileDrag` IPC. The panel uses `buildLineage().exportsOf` and the export runner's state.
- **A copy's page** keeps its "Source" link back to the original.

## Notes for review

- **Seven destinations, as in the design.** Since the export-screen merge, Email is its own card over chat's Balanced preset. The panel lists `DESTINATION_IDS`, so this page and the Export screen can't disagree.
- **The page reads the file for every local recording now**, not only heavy ones, because it needs the resolution, the estimates and each copy's picture size. A copy's picture size is worked out from the original's probe and the copy's preset.
- **The "Saved" notice shows only when the page opened right after a recording** (`fromRecording`). The destinations panel shows whenever an original has no copies and nothing is exporting. "Not now" lasts until you leave the page; nothing is stored.
- **The player's width is capped by the window height**, so at 900 × 670 the actions stay in view. The page scrolls for the panel.
- The `library.*` i18n keys of the old strip are removed, and `copiesEmpty` and `copyProgress*` are replaced. `sendTo` stays, because the Library cards (out of scope here) still use it.
- Backlog: `backlog/prepare-screen.md` and its row in `backlog/index.mdx` are updated. There's no Linear ticket, because the workspace hit its issue limit.

## Verification

`bun run verify` is green: 317 test files, 3091 tests. Nothing has run in Electron yet.

## How to test it yourself

1. Run `bun run rebuild:native` if `bun run setup` asks for it, then `bun run dev` and open the desktop app at its default size (900 × 670).
2. Record a short clip. The page you land on shows `← Library`, the full title, and `MASTER · FULL QUALITY` in one top row, then the metadata line with the resolution.
3. Check the green "Saved to your Library…" notice above the player. Close it with ✕; the line "This is your original. It never changes." appears under the metadata.
4. At the bottom, check "Where is it going?": one row of equal cards, sizes in amber (YouTube, Reels, LinkedIn) or teal (GitHub, Slack, Archive). Click GitHub: Prepare opens with GitHub selected.
5. Go back and click **Not now**. The panel goes away and **Export a copy** appears first among the actions. Click it: Prepare opens with nothing preselected.
6. Export a YouTube copy and return to the original. While it runs, the "Copies from this original" row reads "Exporting · N% · … left" with a bar. When it's done, the row reads "2560 × 1440 · … MB · ✓ Ready".
7. Drag the row's **Drag** handle into Finder. The file lands under the recording's title.
8. Click the copy's name: its page shows "Source" linking back to the original and no master tag.
9. Rename the original to a very long title. It ellipsizes only at the tag, and the action buttons are unaffected.
